subject: Processor vs Service Provider — scope & subprocessor onboarding
messages:
From: Emma Sullivan <emma.sullivan@brighthealth.com>
To: priyom.das@redwood.ai
Cc: Michael Liu <michael.liu@vendorsec.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Mar 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Processor vs Service Provider — scope & subprocessor onboarding

Hi Priyom,

Thanks for taking this. We're in the final stages of BrightHealth's procurement review and have a couple of open items on the privacy annex that need clarification before legal will sign. Attached is our privacy annex (BH_privacy_annex_3.1.pdf) with the specific redlines we expect to see. High level asks:

- Confirm whether Redwood will accept classification as a "service provider" (CCPA/CPRA) for our use case and, if not, explain the operational differences you need to retain.
- Provide a current subprocessor inventory and your onboarding process for emergency/temporary subprocessors. We need onshore fallback options for any CCPA-covered data flows.
- Evidence of transit encryption and KMS practices for telemetry and logs (we're specifically worried about aggregated telemetry that might contain identifiers).
- A reasonable timeline for reviewing/redlining your DPA draft and returning a signed addendum.

We have a short window — procurement wants to close this week if possible. If you can share the DPA redline and subprocessor CSV, that will help speed our internal review.

Thanks,
Emma Sullivan
Sr. Counsel, Data Privacy & Security
BrightHealth

Attachment: BH_privacy_annex_3.1.pdf

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Sullivan <emma.sullivan@brighthealth.com>
Cc: Michael Liu <michael.liu@vendorsec.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 1 Mar 2027 16:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Processor vs Service Provider — scope & subprocessor onboarding

Emma — thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front, then attachments and proposed next steps below.

1) Classification: Redwood is comfortable being treated as a "service provider" (CCPA/CPRA) for the types of API-driven inference and telemetry flows described in your annex. We will accept limited-use, non-retention language for customer-provided PII for the features you are evaluating, provided we can keep transient telemetry for SLO/optimizaton with attestation and allowed retention windows.

2) Subprocessors & onboarding: attached is our current inventory (subprocessor_inventory.csv) and a brief runbook explaining temporary subprocessor activation and emergency onboards. For CCPA-covered data, we have an onshore fallback plan that routes sensitive telemetry to dedicated onshore capacity or a masked telemetry pipeline.

3) Encryption & KMS: transit encryption is TLS 1.3 by default; at-rest uses customer-configurable KMS for Dedicated/Private deployments. For hosted API telemetry we can provide a telemetry attestation (attached: attestation_telemetry.pdf) describing pseudonymization steps we take before long-term storage.

Attachments I am sending: redwood_dpa_draft_v2.docx (clean DPA), subprocessor_inventory.csv, attestation_telemetry.pdf.

Proposed next steps:
- We can accept the service provider addendum language with two carveouts: (a) transient telemetry for performance debugging/metricing (30-day retention default) and (b) operational fallbacks (activated only with notice and limited scope).
- If BrightHealth needs a stricter onshore-only telemetry guarantee, we can offer a Dedicated region lock or on-prem option; I included options and rough pricing in the DPA appendix.
- Happy to do a 30-minute alignment call with procurement/legal + security today or tomorrow to accelerate.

If this aligns, I'll incorporate any specific redline requests you send back and route through Grace and Jonas for approvals on concessions.

Best,
Priyom Das
Senior Manager, Privacy & Contracts
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Processor vs Service Provider — scope & subprocessor onboarding

Priyom / Jonas — quick internal note before we finalize the DPA.

- Limit concessions on telemetry retention: offer 30 days by default with an option for 90-day troubleshooting if BrightHealth signs the telemetry attestation. Do not agree to open-ended retention or deletion exceptions that bypass Customer API controls.
- Subprocessor onboarding: include a clause that emergency/temporary subprocessors will be limited to 90-day activations and require prior notice "where feasible" plus post-activation notification. We can offer SOC 2 Type II reports from the subprocessors where available, but avoid granting audit rights beyond standard contractual checks.
- Escalation path: CC security@redwood into any requests for KMS key handling or custom encryption schemes. If they request onshore-only telemetry at scale, prepare a pricing uplift for Dedicated capacity.

Priyom — integrate these bullet points into the DPA redline and ping me for a final sign-off before sending to Emma.

Thanks,
Grace O'Connor
VP, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

Priyom / Grace — this is helpful, thank you. We reviewed the DPA draft and the subprocessor CSV — a couple of quick clarifications:

- BrightHealth accepts the "service provider" classification with the telemetry attestation language included (attestation_telemetry.pdf).
- We need the emergency subprocessor notification language to include a maximum notification window (we propose 48 hours post-activation where notice could not be provided in advance).
- Please add a short clause referencing encryption in transit: "TLS 1.3 or better; mutual TLS available for Dedicated deployments."

If you can incorporate the 48-hour notification and the explicit mTLS sentence, we'll route through our signatories and send a DocuSign later today. Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Best regards,
Emma Sullivan
Sr. Counsel, Data Privacy & Security
BrightHealth
